chunks: Ali, from his father, from Dawood Al Nahdy, from one of our companions who said:

Ibn Abu Saeed Al-Mukari came to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May Allah grant you the capacity to claim what your father claimed.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'What is the matter with you? May Allah extinguish your light and bring poverty into your house. Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Imran, 'I shall endow you with a male,' so He endowed him with Maryam, and endowed Maryam with Isa (peace be upon him). Thus Isa is from Maryam, and Maryam is from Isa, and Maryam and Isa are one thing; and I am from my father, and my father is from me, and I and my father are one thing.'
He said, 'So he left from his presence, became poor until he died, and did not have the means for an overnight stay. May Allah curse him.'

Ibn Abu Saeed said to him, 'And I ask you a question.' He said, 'I do not think you will accept from me, and you are not from my flock, but come with it.' He said: 'A man said upon his death, 'Every slave of mine who is old, he is free for the Face of Allah.' He said, 'Yes. Allah, Mighty is His Mention, says in His Book, 'Until it becomes like an old dry palm branch.' Thus whatever was from his slaves, upon whom six months have passed, is considered old, and he is free.'
He (the narrator) said, 'So he went out from his presence, and contemplated until he died, and there did not happen to be an overnight stay. May Allah curse him.'

key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: The one who claims or boasts

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'old' slave for emancipation in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) engages Ibn Abu Saeed in a dialectical refutation of the claim of mutual generation (takaful) between Maryam and Isa, using the Quranic narrative of their miraculous creation to illustrate that while they are distinct entities linked by divine will, the Imam and his father Ali are ontologically one in essence and lineage. This encounter highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the spiritual and physical continuity of the Imams, contrasting it with the specific miracle of Mary and Jesus. The hadith concludes with the immediate divine retribution of poverty upon Ibn Abu Saeed, serving as a practical sign of the Imam's authority.
